known.title: Cursor CLI
known.reason: it signs in with a Cursor account, which Dozer cannot hold on the Mac for it yet

known.title: Crush
known.reason: its licence (FSL-1.1-MIT) forbids competing uses until each release turns MIT two years on, so Dozer needs a legal reading before it installs it for you; technically it runs (0.98.1 answered a turn on an xAI key in a sandbox)

known.title: MiMo Code
known.reason: its code is MIT, but it comes with Xiaomi's own use restrictions, which need a reading before Dozer installs it for you; technically it runs (0.1.15 answered a turn on an xAI key in a sandbox, its usage tracking off)

known.title: JetBrains Junie CLI
known.reason: a Java application in a 340 MB release folder: Dozer installs one program file, and its bundled Java runtime does not trust the sandbox's certificate authority yet; its own-key mode (an xAI key, no JetBrains account) reached xAI in a sandbox once both were done by hand

known.title: ForgeCode
known.reason: it no longer reads an API key from the environment: it copies the key into its own credentials file, where the placeholder Dozer gives each session would go stale — Dozer has no per-session way to write it there yet

known.title: jcode
known.reason: its linux-arm64 build needs glibc 2.38 or later (Ubuntu 24.04); Dozer's agent images are on Debian 12 (glibc 2.36), and an agent on the Ubuntu base is not set up yet

known.title: Amp
known.reason: its models run only through Amp's own service, with an Amp API key (sgamp_…), which Dozer cannot hold for you yet

known.title: Kiro CLI
known.reason: it runs only on Kiro's own models, with a Kiro API key from a paid plan (Pro and above) or an AWS sign-in, which Dozer cannot hold for you yet

known.title: Qoder CLI
known.reason: it signs in with a Qoder personal access token, which Dozer cannot hold for you yet; its own-model mode is set inside its interface and may need a paid plan

known.title: Poolside pool
known.reason: installing it means agreeing to Poolside's end-user licence on your behalf, which needs a reading first; and it runs on Poolside's own models with a Poolside key or an OpenRouter sign-in

known.title: Aider
known.reason: its current release (0.86.2) needs Python 3.10 to 3.12; the Python Dozer installs tools into is 3.13

known.title: Kode
known.reason: it keeps the model's API key in its own settings file (~/.kode.json; an imported fromEnv key is copied in as text), where the placeholder Dozer gives each session would go stale — Dozer has no per-session way to write it there yet
